method: hub = highest IN-REGION degree (not total, not outward — the Axis Gate case). gate = not the hub, >=3 outward, and outward > 2x in-region. parent = in-region neighbour with highest in-region degree, ties toward the hub. tier = region for the hub, settlement if it has dependents, site if it is a leaf.

aeviReview.summary: 27 flagged, all answered. ⛔ 20 of your 24 cross-region rows were ONE finding: the foothills are the waystation network. Every one names its own span in its worldPosNote and all 22 parse cleanly. ⚠️ CORRECTED AGAIN BY ERIK: they are `tier: settlement` with `role: waypoint`, not a waypoint TIER. TIER IS SIZE, ROLE IS FUNCTION — the same rule I gave you for `gate` and then broke myself one paragraph later. They are real towns that happen to sit at midpoints; parentId stays null because a waypoint belongs to a ROUTE, not to a hub.
aeviReview.newTier: `waypoint` — a location defined by the route it sits on rather than the place it belongs to. parentId null, spans [start,end]. ⚠️ It is why the foothills span 277 walking days and why that is correct.
aeviReview.openReturned: `gate` stays a ROLE. World view draws tier:region PLUS role:gate — a render rule, not a taxonomy change.
aeviReview.reRun: the_old_warden_post and the_hollowing both changed region AFTER your run (4189e260, f1c90c62). Re-derive those two.
aeviReview.tierVsRole: ⛔ THE RULE, stated once so neither of us breaks it again: TIER answers HOW BIG AND WHAT CONTAINS IT — region, settlement, site. ROLE answers WHAT IT DOES — gate, waypoint. A place can carry one tier and any number of roles. ⚠️ Anything that forces a choice between two true facts about a place is a tier that should have been a role.
